result.effect: heritability 64% (95% CI 0.41–0.91); common factor captured 66–100% of each test's heritability

cells.quote: The six tests correlated substantially and clustered into one common factor, capturing between 32 and 57% of the variance in each individual test, which we named ‘Navigation’, as it indexed abilities that are generally described in the literature as spatial navigation skills
cells.note: Factor-analytic and twin-model association; no instructional comparison was manipulated.

O.outcome_detail: performance across training sessions associated with right inferior parietal cortical thickness

cells.quote: Legault and colleagues found that cortical thickness, a structural brain measure of gray-matter thickness from the surface of the cortex to the white matter, is associated with different contexts of learning: after 2– 3 weeks of intensive L2 vocabulary training across seven sessions, the VR learners showed a positive correlation in the right IPL with performance across all training sessions, while the non-VR learners showed a positive correlation at the final stages only in the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), a region associated with effective explicit language training 58 (though there is counter evidence59).
cells.note: The study reports within-group correlations and different brain regions or training stages, not a direct between-condition effect estimate.

cells.quote: The main challenge identified in ML2 learning is the need for immersive, interactive experiences that engage students and enhance their learning outcomes. All 25 participants agreed that VR’s immersive nature can be leveraged to enhance student engagement in ML2 lessons.

cells.quote: VR can provide interactive experiences that can help students improve their Maltese language skills. VR encourages communication, and that is what our foreign students mostly need when learning Maltese. Currently, we cannot give them this kind of experience in the classroom or online.
cells.note: This is a teacher-reported anticipated benefit, not a measured comparison; participants had not used Maltese VR applications.

cells.quote: According to 20 participants, VR can provide a real or virtual tour based on lessons intended to help students build language skills and apply them in authentic contexts, as Teacher 7 explained: A VR game can give the one-of-a-kind, immersive experience that many learners of Maltese seek—namely, the opportunity to use their language skills in an authentic context.
